thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden org traffic spike detected for org=ORG-592. 5m ago baseline qps-> 45k, now 180k. p99 latency 3800ms. Errors 5xx rising. Auto-suppress not triggered. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

oncall-alice: I'm on it. Acknowledging incident. Anyone from infra or SRE able to join?

sre-ben: I'll be there. Can we get the affected call patterns? embeddings/streaming/long-context?

infra-lee: Logs indicate lots of long-context chat completions and streaming sessions topping out caches. Most traffic from a single org key (ORG-592). No infra-wide CPU/GPU saturation – it's org-specific.

product-jordan: If this is sustained the customer's latency/SLA will hit. Need a mitigation that minimizes downstream user-facing failures.

acct-maya: Heads-up: ORG-592 is a strategic customer on Dedicated pilot. They'll expect a heads-up before any perf-impacting change. I'll draft a quick message if we decide to throttle.

oncall-alice: Options: 1) temporarily tighten org concurrency/quota, 2) disable nonessential features for that org (e.g., search embeddings), 3) route to cheaper model variant with lower throughput. Preference for (1) + (2) short window. Thoughts?

sre-ben: Agree. We can enact a temporary quota cut to 25% of their normal QPS and add a sliding window to auto-restore after 30m if stable. I'll prepare the admin command.

infra-lee: We'll also flip prefix caching to aggressive for that org to help tails. Minimal customer-visible change.

oncall-alice: Maya — send the short note in parallel. Ben, paste the exact command you plan to run and I'll execute.

sre-ben: Running via admin API. Command to apply 25% concurrency and 30m TTL: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/orgs/ORG-592/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"override_type":"concurrency_cut","value":0.25,"ttl_seconds":1800,"reason":"emergency org spike 3612340987"}'
```

oncall-alice: Executing now.

infra-lee: Also executing cache mode: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/orgs/ORG-592/cache_mode" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"mode":"aggressive","ttl_seconds":1800}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION: override applied for ORG-592 by oncall-alice. concurrency_cut=0.25 ttl=1800s. cache_mode=aggressive ttl=1800s. (event_id=evt_3612340987_1) :white_check_mark:

acct-maya: Sent: "We're seeing a traffic surge impacting latency. We'll apply a short protective limit for ~30 minutes to stabilize performance, then reevaluate. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause." Customer ops replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted."

product-jordan: Monitoring graphs?

infra-lee: p95/p99 dropping. Error rate down from 4.8% -> 0.9% within 2 minutes. Latency p99 down to ~450ms. Good.

oncall-alice: Nice. Keep watch for 15min, then we can consider gradual relaxation to 50% for another 30m. Ben, create a follow-up ticket for postmortem and capacity plan.

sre-ben: Created ticket INF-1482: "ORG-592 emergency spike — mitigation & follow-up". Assigning to infra team for root cause and to product for potential rate-limiting policy adjustments.

acct-maya: I'll keep CS looped and schedule a post-incident customer sync.

incident-bot: REMINDER: auto-override TTL expires in 25m unless extended.

oncall-alice: If spike recurs, we'll switch to stepwise ramping and consider model variant fallback. For now monitoring looks stable. Closing this paging thread — moving to incident channel for follow-up. :thumbsup:
